rounds.text: Mehta Securities Ltd is showing undeniable green shoots of a powerful operational turnaround that the market has yet to fully appreciate. Trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth has surged to 50% [E16], backed by screen reasons highlighting strong sales growth [E47] and year-over-year surges [E46]. Furthermore, the operating margin has staged a dramatic recovery to 21% in the TTM period, marking a massive 107 percentage point expansion from -86% three years earlier [E26], alongside a quarterly operating margin improvement of 108 percentage points compared to the year-ago quarter [E27]. Confidence from insiders is growing concurrently, with promoter holding increasing by 1.54 percentage points from 72.09% in Sep 2023 to 73.63% in Jun 2026 [E35]. The company remains conservatively financed with a modest debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21x [E32], and the underlying business results score an impressive 95 out of 100 with accelerating net profit growth up 86% year-over-year [E53]. Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E12], [E14], [E30], [E37].

The valuation of Mehta Securities Ltd is entirely disconnected from its fundamental delivery, trading at an exorbitant P/E ratio of 114x alongside a sector-dwarfing EV/EBITDA of 112.7x [E1, E6, E11]. This extreme multiple is completely unsupported by historical performance, characterized by a miserable 5-year compounded sales contraction of -13% and a 10-year median ROE of -3% [E14, E22]. The disconnect is brutally quantified by a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 3 per share against a market price of Rs 22, resulting in an alarming -581.0% margin of safety [E37, E38]. Furthermore, the business is actively cash-destructive, generating negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.34 Cr each as of March 2026 while compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months sits at -63% [E17, E30, E31]. The reverse DCF model confirms that current pricing aggressively prices in an unsustainable 31.8% earnings growth, leaving the stock vulnerable to severe multiple contraction [E39]. conceded: [E16]

The bear relies heavily on lofty historical multiples like a P/E of 114x and an EV/EBITDA of 112.7x, yet ignores that price-to-book sits at a modest 1.23x, closely aligned with the sector benchmark of 1.29x [E1, E2, E6, E7, E11]. While the bear points to historical sales contractions and negative median ROE over trailing periods, it overlooks powerful recent operational acceleration, including a stellar 50% compounded trailing-twelve-month sales growth and a dramatic margin expansion of 107 percentage points in operating margin to 21% [E14, E16, E22, E26, E46, E47]. Furthermore, insider conviction completely contradicts the notion of a broken enterprise: promoters have actively increased their stake to 73.63% [E35]. The business maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a low debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.21x [E32]. Finally, dismissals of the stock based on stale sentiment fail to recognize that current results score an impressive 95/100 on turnaround metrics [E53]. conceded: [E17, E30, E31, E37, E38]

The bull celebrates a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.23x, but this ignores the staggering operational reality that a P/B near parity is attached to an enterprise with an ROE of 0.0%, an ROCE of 0.05%, and a 10-year median ROE of -3% [E2, E9, E10, E13, E22]. While the bull highlights a TTM sales growth surge of 50%, it conveniently overlooks that compounded sales growth over the past five years sits at -13% and that TTM profit growth collapsed by 63% [E14, E16, E17, E46]. The argument that promoters increased their stake to 73.63% fails to offset the severe fundamental cash drain of operating and free cash flows standing at negative Rs 0.34 Cr in March 2026 alongside rising borrowings [E30, E31, E33, E35]. Conceded: [E26, E32, E53]. Dismissing the DCF valuation warning of a -581% margin of safety is dangerous when a reverse DCF demands an aggressive 31.8% earnings growth just to justify the current price [E37, E38, E39, E51].
